messages.text: Monday, September 28 · Canton, Michigan
Autumn air, a full moon rising, and local histories on display
A partly cloudy autumn day offers a high near 76°F. Local history is on display in Ypsilanti, while science explores the early assembly of our own galaxy.
Expect partly cloudy skies today with a high near 76°F and a low around 51°F.
Sunrise is at 7:28 AM, sunset at 7:20 PM, with a full moon 96.9% illuminated.
Local happenings and cultural notes

In Ypsilanti, the YDL-Superior is featuring the Ypsi Farmers & Gardeners Oral History Exhibit, offering a free look at local food growers. For music lovers, Spiral Galaxy performs at Trinosophes in Detroit at 7:30 PM.
Mark your calendar for September 30, which is My Birthday and Patrick's Birthday.
Ann Arbor's fiscal plans and U-M's cancer research

Ann Arbor City Council has approved a spending plan for funds from a downtown property sale, allocating $14.2 million to $17.4 million across 12 projects. The University of Michigan has also established a $10 million center to advance soundwave cancer treatments.
Tomorrow's events and learning opportunities
Tomorrow offers a fireside chat on Black Reading Month at Howard Family Bookstore in Detroit at 6 PM, and an interactive workshop on AI for everyday use at Farmington Library at 6 PM.
Space telescope finds ancient galactic collision

NASA's Hubble telescope has identified evidence of an ancient collision with a dwarf galaxy that shaped the Milky Way's early assembly. Additionally, NASA's Starling satellites have demonstrated GPS-free autonomous navigation in orbit.
The next Starship orbital flight attempt is estimated no earlier than September 18, 2026.
A quiet afternoon can hold a universe of discovery.
Tuesday, September 29 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast skies, soundwave cancer research, and a Detroit film premiere

Tuesday dawns overcast with a warm high near 75°F. Locally, the University of Michigan's $10 million investment in soundwave cancer treatments is a significant scientific advancement. For evening plans, consider the premiere of 'Etched In Pavement' in Detroit.
Today will be overcast with a high near 75°F and a low around 49°F, with no chance of precipitation.
Sunrise is at 7:29 AM, with sunset at 7:19 PM; the moon is a waning gibbous, 91.9% illuminated.
Tonight's nearby happenings

The 'Etched In Pavement' documentary film premiere is tonight at 7:00 PM at the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History in Detroit. For comedy fans, Colin Mochrie & Brad Sherwood perform at 7:30 PM at Sound Board at MotorCity Casino Hotel.
Tomorrow is My Birthday and Patrick's Birthday.
University of Michigan advances cancer treatment research

The University of Michigan has established a $10 million Histotripsy Center to advance non-invasive cancer treatments using soundwaves. This technique, already FDA-approved for liver tumors, uses targeted soundwaves to break apart tumors without surgery or radiation.
Looking ahead to Wednesday
Tomorrow, consider Alexis N. Nelson speaking at the U-M School of Environment and Sustainability for 'Foraging a Better Future,' or enjoy live music from Horse Lords at Trinosophes in Detroit.
NASA satellites navigate without GPS, Roman telescope readies for launch

NASA's Starling satellites have demonstrated autonomous navigation using onboard cameras and a catalog of space objects, eliminating the need for GPS. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has cleared its flight-readiness review and is proceeding to final launch preparations.
SpaceX’s launch page does not list an official Flight 14 date; independent estimates place the next orbital Starship attempt no earlier than September 18, 2026.
A quiet observation can lead to a day's worth of discovery.
